scope: language-conditioned MiniMax-H3 robot-action generation in an existing real flower scene
summary: A real-video scene-anchor route produced three frame-aligned MiniMax-H3 robot videos whose insert, handover, and inspect language conditions remain measurably distinct after five agentic repair rounds, but strict identity and semantic-action acceptance remain unmet.
evidence: outputs/minimax-h3-action-control/20260810T051500Z-anchor-action-v2/metadata.json records three completed 124-frame NF4 H3 inferences on physical A800 GPU 7 with pinned DiffSynth b1c02ce, 20 steps, and seed 20260810

outputs/minimax-h3-action-control/20260810T051500Z-anchor-action-v2/comparison/action-comparison.json records pairwise post-repair full-frame MADs 3.0356, 6.2584, and 6.5564 with all outputs numerically distinct
All three selected repairs have background and object locks approximately 1.0, subject replacement approximately 0.8997, and source-face replacement above 0.9997
The 832x588 four-way comparison contains 124 aligned frames at 24 FPS and has SHA-256 75603a7ab70669b4dbb3a0f7e3e54deb802ea890360afafdf0a30b485a57a365
The browser demo publishes the real source, all three selected H3 videos, their commands and timelines, the matched comparison, and an explicit PARTIAL evidence panel
lessons: Using one scene anchor extracted from the real video removes source-person temporal dominance while retaining a real camera and workspace reference.
Action-override evaluation must exclude source-motion preservation from candidate selection because divergence from the source person's action is intentional.
Numerical distinctness and background safety are necessary but do not establish exact semantic compliance with insertion, hand transfer, or wrist rotation.
limitations: Robot-identity proxies of 0.5975-0.6123 remain below the 0.72 gate, so every strict action candidate is rejected.
Complete human review of exact insertion, right-to-left transfer, and 45-degree wrist rotation is pending.
The model uses third-party NF4 MiniMax-H3 weights rather than official BF16 weights.
This is a 5.17-second image-space world-model demonstration, not contact physics or real-robot execution.
next_actions: Add action-specific pose/contact evaluation or human labels, then regenerate weak variants with explicit spatial keyframes and accept only commands that pass semantic review.
Run the same matched comparison with official BF16 weights when their verified checkpoint and sufficient GPU memory are available.
